summary: AnalogScope is a transparent, multi-criteria method for finding and ranking Earth locations that mimic Moon and Mars conditions. It scores a candidate site from 0 to 5 on eight dimensions: geology, terrain, temperature extremes, water and ice, dust and wind, habitability, subsurface features, and operations. A weighted sum then gives an AnalogScore from 0 to 100, with different weights for Moon and Mars goals. For every site we also record a mismatch register of what Earth cannot reproduce, such as gravity, radiation and atmosphere. We tested it on three lesser-used sites. Ladakh (India) is the strongest all-round analog, scoring 78 for Mars. The Danakil Depression (Ethiopia) is the best Mars habitability analog, and Lanzarote's lava tubes (Spain) are the best lunar shelter analog. Next, we will replace our expert-judgement scores with computed layers from NASA Earth data and LRO/MRO data, and build an interactive web map with adjustable weights.
details: AnalogScope is a transparent method for finding and ranking Earth locations that mimic Moon and Mars conditions. It scores a candidate site from 0 to 5 on eight dimensions (geology, terrain, temperature, water and ice, dust and wind, habitability, subsurface features, operations), and a weighted sum gives an AnalogScore from 0 to 100, with separate weights for Moon and Mars goals. Every site also gets a mismatch register of what Earth cannot reproduce, such as gravity, radiation and atmosphere. We screened Lanzarote lava tubes (Spain), the Danakil Depression (Ethiopia) and Ladakh (India). Ladakh is the best all-round analog, Danakil the best Mars habitability analog, and Lanzarote the best lunar lava-tube analog. The scores are a proof of concept based on expert judgement. Next, we will compute them from NASA Earth data, LRO and MRO layers, score a global grid, and publish an interactive web map with adjustable weights. Tools: Python, QGIS and NASA open data.
